questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians. Even when you have a green light, you must be careful and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is driving closely behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she passes.
Speed up as he or she passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact. Speeding up or blocking the lane will make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you to a possible train. Obey all railroad warning signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means traffic is merging from the right side.

questions.question: Florida law requires you to use headlights:

options.text: To get the attention of other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Florida law requires you to use headlights from sunset to sunrise. Drive with extra care at night.

questions.question: Another driver cuts you off in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely. This helps prevent road rage.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. If your car has fog lights, use them too. High beams bounce off the fog and reduce your visibility.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only used in construction zones.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers important information. They show where to position your vehicle, where it is safe to pass, and warn about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is in your area. What should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle and block its path.
Give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
Signal to them when it is clear to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
questions.explanation: Make every effort to give an emergency vehicle a clear path. If safe, pull your vehicle to the side of the road so they can pass.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to signal a turn?
questions.explanation: Use hand signals to tell other drivers you are turning when your vehicle's turn signals do not work.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones. They are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols and warn that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a travel lane?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance ramp.
Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, go to the next one or find a safe place to turn around.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, park within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: What effect does smoking while driving have?

options.text: It does not affect your driving.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by making you take your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out while you are driving?

options.text: Steer straight and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake until you have control. Then brake gently and pull off the road at a safe location.

questions.question: You are in the right lane and want to move left. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: When can you drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing?

options.text: If a train is not too close.
If your vehicle will not damage the gate.
If you look both ways first.

questions.explanation: When you see flashing red lights, a lowered gate, or bells at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights stop, the bells stop, and the gate is fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: When you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting a freeway. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: On a long trip, what helps prevent driver fatigue?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and take a nap or find a place to sleep.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is an available passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You may also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Slow down, move to the side to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the side to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, slow down, create a clear path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and make sure all passengers keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to exit. Wait for the officer to ask you for your driver license, registration, and insurance cards.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Decreases the number of driving errors.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes more driving errors.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously, stay calm and increase the distance between your vehicles. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal in the direction you want to move. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and the far lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see better.

questions.explanation: Fog reduces visibility of other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive slowly and reduce your speed. Do not use high beam headlights. Use low beams to better see the road and objects ahead.
